blocks.text: Practice long questions for the whole of Unit 2 (Functions and Graphs), in the shape of a Board Section-II question part: each carries 5 marks (a longer problem, a proof or a derivation). Each one is solved in full, step by step.

blocks.explanation: Replace every \(x\) by the given input, using brackets, then simplify.

book_ref.quote: is called the value of \(f\) at \(x\)

steps: Collect like terms: \(f(x - 1) = x^{3} - x^{2} - 2x + 5\). Check: at \(x = 1\) it gives \(3 = f(0)\).

blocks.prompt: 2 Find the domain and range of \(f(x) = \frac{x}{x^{2} + x - 6}\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Remove the zeros of the denominator; for the range write \(y = f(x)\) and ask for which \(y\) a real \(x\) exists.

book_ref.quote: Domain: where is the denominator zero?

steps: \(y = 0\) gives \(x = 0\), which is in the domain.
For \(y \ne 0\) the discriminant is \((y - 1)^{2} + 24y^{2} > 0\) (a square plus a positive term), so a real \(x\) always exists.
That \(x\) is never \(2\) or \(-3\): putting \(x = 2\) gives \(4y + 2y - 2 - 6y = -2 \ne 0\), and \(x = -3\) gives \(9y - 3y + 3 - 6y = 3 \ne 0\). Range \(= \mathbb{R}\).

blocks.prompt: 3 Find the domain and range of \(f(x) = \sqrt{x^{2} - 2x - 8}\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: The quantity under the root must be \(\ge 0\); solve that inequality with critical points and test values.

book_ref.quote: Condition for a real square root

steps: On the domain \(x^{2} - 2x - 8\) takes the value \(0\) (at \(-2\) and \(4\)) and grows without bound as \(x \to \pm\infty\).

blocks.prompt: 4 Find the domain and range of \(f(x) = \frac{1}{x^{2} + 2}\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: The denominator is never zero; bound it from below, then turn the fraction over.

book_ref.quote: Every real number can be squared

steps: \(x^{2} \ge 0 \Rightarrow x^{2} + 2 \ge 2 > 0\): the denominator is never zero, so domain \(= \mathbb{R}\).
The largest value \(\frac{1}{2}\) comes at \(x = 0\); \(f(x) > 0\) always, and \(f(x) \to 0\) as \(x\) grows, but never equals \(0\).
For \(0 < y \le \frac{1}{2}\): \(x^{2} = \frac{1}{y} - 2 \ge 0\) gives a real \(x\). Range \(= \left(0, \frac{1}{2}\right]\).

blocks.explanation: Prove one-to-one (equal outputs force equal inputs) and onto (solve \(y = f(x)\) for \(x\)).

book_ref.quote: is called bijective if it is both one-to-one and onto.

steps: Then \(-4x_{1} = -4x_{2} \Rightarrow x_{1} = x_{2}\). So \(f\) is one-to-one.
Onto: take any \(y \in \mathbb{R}\) and solve \(y = 7 - 4x\): \(x = \frac{7 - y}{4} \in \mathbb{R}\).
Check: \(f\left(\frac{7 - y}{4}\right) = 7 - (7 - y) = y\). Every \(y\) has a pre-image, so \(f\) is onto.
Being both one-to-one and onto, \(f\) is bijective.
blocks.final_answer: \(f\) is one-to-one and onto, hence bijective

blocks.prompt: 6 Show that \(f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}\), \(f(x) = x^{2} + 4x\) is neither one-to-one nor onto. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Find two inputs with the same output; then complete the square to find the least value and a co-domain element left out.

book_ref.quote: This means that no two different elements of the domain map to the same element of the co-domain.

steps: Two different inputs give the same output, so \(f\) is not one-to-one.
Take \(-5\) in the co-domain: \((x + 2)^{2} - 4 = -5 \Rightarrow (x + 2)^{2} = -1\), no real root.
\(-5\) has no pre-image; the range is not all of \(\mathbb{R}\), so \(f\) is not onto.

blocks.prompt: 7 Let \(X = Y = [0, \infty)\). Prove that \(f : X \to Y\), \(f(x) = x^{2}\) is bijective. Why does the same rule fail on \(\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}\)? (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: The type of a function depends on its domain and co-domain, not only on the rule.

book_ref.quote: has at least one pre-image in the domain

steps: If \(x_{1} + x_{2} = 0\) with both \(\ge 0\), then \(x_{1} = x_{2} = 0\); otherwise \(x_{1} = x_{2}\). So \(f\) is one-to-one on \(X\).
Onto: for any \(y \ge 0\), \(x = \sqrt{y} \in X\) and \(f(\sqrt{y}) = y\). So \(f\) is onto \(Y\); hence bijective.
And \(-1\) has no pre-image (\(x^{2} = -1\) has no real root), so not onto.
blocks.final_answer: Bijective on \([0, \infty)\); neither one-to-one nor onto on \(\mathbb{R}\)

blocks.explanation: First decide which piece each input belongs to; then find the outputs of each piece on its own interval.

book_ref.quote: Each piece applies to a specific part of the domain.

blocks.prompt: 9 Find the points where the line \(y = -3x + 9\) meets the coordinate axes, using a table of values, and draw its graph. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: On the \(x\)-axis \(y = 0\); on the \(y\)-axis \(x = 0\); a line needs only two points.

book_ref.quote: Find the points of intersection of a linear function

steps: Plot \((0, 9)\), \((1, 6)\), \((2, 3)\), \((3, 0)\) and join them by a straight line falling to the right (slope \(-3\)).

blocks.prompt: 10 Find the point of intersection of \(y = 2x - 3\) and \(y = -2x + 9\) by a table of values, and confirm it algebraically. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: In one table, the row where the two \(y\)-values are equal gives the point.

book_ref.quote: The point of intersection of two linear functions is the point where their graphs cross each other.

steps: At \(x = 3\) both give \(y = 3\): the point is \((3, 3)\).

blocks.prompt: 11 Find the points of intersection of \(y = x + 1\) and \(y = x^{2} - 2x - 3\). Also find the vertex of the parabola. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Equate the two \(y\)'s to get a quadratic; each real root gives one meeting point.

book_ref.quote: If there are two solutions, the system has two points of intersection.

blocks.prompt: 12 Find where the line \(y = x\) meets the parabola \(y = -x^{2} + 4x\). Give the vertex of the parabola and say whether it opens up or down. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Equate and factor; the sign of \(a\) decides the opening.

book_ref.quote: The vertex \((h, k)\) of the parabola

steps: \(a = -1 < 0\), so the parabola opens downward and \((2, 4)\) is its highest point.

blocks.prompt: 13 Show that \(y = 4x - 4\) touches \(y = x^{2}\) at exactly one point, and that \(y = 4x - 5\) does not meet it at all. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Form the quadratic for each line; the discriminant tells how many meeting points there are.

book_ref.quote: If no solution exists, it means the line and the parabola do not intersect.

steps: \((x - 2)^{2} = 0\): only \(x = 2\), \(y = 4\). One point \((2, 4)\): the line is a tangent.
No real root: \(y = 4x - 5\) and \(y = x^{2}\) do not intersect (the line lies below the parabola, e.g. at \(x = 2\): \(3 < 4\)).
blocks.final_answer: Tangent at \((2, 4)\); \(y = 4x - 5\) has no common point

blocks.prompt: 14 Find the domain and range of \(y = 3\sqrt{x} - 1\). Make a table for \(x = 0, 1, 4, 9\), find \(y\) at \(x = 2\), and describe the graph. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Choose perfect squares for \(x\) so the roots are exact; the least value is at \(x = 0\).

book_ref.quote: Plot the points of the table and join them with a smooth curve

steps: Plot \((0, -1)\), \((1, 2)\), \((2, 3.24)\), \((4, 5)\), \((9, 8)\) and join by a smooth curve starting at \((0, -1)\), rising ever more slowly.

blocks.prompt: 15 Find the domain and range of \(y = \sqrt[3]{x} + 2\). Make a table for \(x = -8, -1, 0, 1, 8\) and find where the graph meets the axes. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Use perfect cubes for exact values; a cube root exists for negative numbers too.

book_ref.quote: because the cube root of any number (positive, negative or zero) is always real

steps: Every real number has a real cube root, so the domain is all real numbers.
Any \(y\) comes from \(x = (y - 2)^{3}\), so the range is all real numbers.
Plot the points and join by a smooth S-shaped curve through \((0, 2)\), extending on both sides.
blocks.final_answer: Domain and range all reals; meets axes at \((0, 2)\) and \((-8, 0)\)

blocks.prompt: 16 A stock worth Rs. 8,000 grows at 6% per year as \(P(t) = P_{0}e^{rt}\). Find (i) its value after 5 years, (ii) its doubling time, (iii) its value after 20 years. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Write the rate as a decimal; for doubling set \(P = 2P_{0}\) and take \(\ln\).

book_ref.quote: The value of a stock follows the exponential growth model

steps: Check: \(20\) years is less than two doubling times (\(23.1\)), and \(26561 < 4 \times 8000 = 32000\).

blocks.prompt: 17 A concentration decays as \(C(t) = \frac{120}{\sqrt{t + 4}}\) ppm, \(t\) in days. Find (i) \(C(0)\) and \(C(5)\), (ii) after how many days it is below \(15\) ppm. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Substitute for (i); for (ii) solve the equality, then use that \(C\) decreases.

book_ref.quote: When something decreases in quantity or size over time, it is called decay.

steps: As \(t\) grows, \(\sqrt{t + 4}\) grows, so \(C(t)\) decreases: after 60 days \(C < 15\) ppm (e.g. \(C(96) = \frac{120}{10} = 12\)).
